Takes an sdid() object and plots the treated and synthetic control trajectories along with the lambda weights conveying which pre-treatment periods were most informative for predicting post-treatment outcomes among the controls.

Source: R/plot.R
sdid_plot.Rd

Two plotting styles are available: "minimal" and "effects". Its default, style = 'minimal', plots both trajectories in black, with the treatment line being solid and synthetic line dashed. The time weights are plotted as a gray band with their scale on a right-hand axis, while the last pre-treatment period is plotted a vertical red dashed line. The alternative, style = 'effects' adds a diff-in-diff diagram conveying the treatment effect while reducing the trajectory lines opacity.

sdid_plot(
  estimates,
  treated.name = "treated",
  control.name = "synthetic control",
  spaghetti.units = c(),
  spaghetti.matrices = NULL,
  lambda.comparable = FALSE,
  overlay = 0,
  lambda.plot.scale = 3,
  effect.curvature = 0.3,
  line.width = 0.5,
  point.size = 1,
  onset.alpha = 0.8,
  spaghetti.line.width = 0.2,
  spaghetti.label.size = 2,
  spaghetti.line.alpha = 0.3,
  spaghetti.label.alpha = 0.5,
  alpha.multiplier = NULL,
  style = c("minimal", "effects"),
  lambda.axis = TRUE,
  x.breaks = NULL,
  y.breaks = NULL
)

Arguments

estimates

The result of an sdid object or a list of sdid estimates. For a staggered sdid result, each adoption period is plotted in a stacked panel.

treated.name

A string conveying the name of the treated curve that appears in the legend. Defaults to "treated".

control.name

A string conveying the name of the control curve that appears in the legend. Defaults to 'synthetic control'.

spaghetti.units

A list of units to plot individually alongside the treatment and control curves. Defaults to the empty list.

spaghetti.matrices

A list of matrices, one for each element of estimates, of trajectories to plot individually. The rows of these matrices should be the same length as the trajectories in Y and they must be named so trajectories can be labeled in the plot.

lambda.comparable

Logical argument where if TRUE, the lambda weight axis is scaled to range from 0 to 1. Useful for when comparing across stacked panels. Defaults to FALSE.

overlay

A number between 0 and 1 that shifts the synthetic control toward the treated trajectory by that fraction of the difference in their time-weighted pre-treatment averages. At 0, the default, both are drawn as estimated. Values near 1 bring them close, which makes it easier to judge whether they move in parallel, and at 1 they overlap and the effects diagram is left out, as for a synthetic control estimate. An estimate's own value can be set as its attribute "overlay". A vector draws the plot at each value, marked by the frame aesthetic, which plotly shows as an animation.

lambda.plot.scale

A number setting the height of the time weights' band, the range of the trajectories divided by this number. Defaults to 3.

effect.curvature

A number setting the curvature of the arrow that marks the effect in the effects style. Defaults to 0.3.

line.width

A number setting the width of the trajectory lines. Defaults to 0.5.

point.size

A number setting the size of the points in the effects style's diagram. Defaults to 1.

onset.alpha

A number between 0 and 1 setting the opacity of the red dashed line marking the start of treatment, drawn midway between the last period before treatment and the first treated period. Defaults to 0.8.

spaghetti.line.width

A number setting the width of the trajectories drawn by spaghetti.units and spaghetti.matrices. Defaults to 0.2.

spaghetti.label.size

A number setting the size of their labels. Defaults to 2.

spaghetti.line.alpha

A number between 0 and 1 setting the opacity of those trajectories. Defaults to 0.3.

spaghetti.label.alpha

A number between 0 and 1 setting the opacity of their labels. Defaults to 0.5.

alpha.multiplier

A vector with one number per estimate, multiplying the opacity of everything drawn for that estimate, to emphasize some estimates over others. Defaults to 1 for every estimate.

style

The plot's style, "minimal" (the default) or "effects". See Details.

lambda.axis

Logical argument where if TRUE, each panel with a time weights' band shows the band's scale on a right-hand axis. Defaults to TRUE.

x.breaks, y.breaks

Optional ticks for the time and outcome axes, as numbers, or as dates for a time axis of dates. A numeric axis runs between its outermost ticks, widened to cover the data if needed, and the frame, padding, cohort labels and time weights' band follow them. The band's baseline sits on the highest outcome tick below it, if there is one, and with stacked panels the outcome ticks apply to every panel. A time axis of dates uses the given dates as ticks and keeps the range of the data. Prefer these to adding a scale to the returned plot, which replaces the one it sets.

Value

A ggplot object, which draws the plot when printed and can be extended with +, for example with labels, themes or further layers. Scales, facets and coordinate systems added this way replace those the plot sets, as described above.

Details

Feeding a staggered treatment sdid() object plots cohort panels stacked in a column and are identified by their adoption periods, labeled under each panel at that period. Adding your own x- or y-scale to the returned plot replaces the one this function sets, and with it the time-weight axis or the x padding. Adding facets or a coordinate system misplaces the time-weight axes of stacked panels. If a list of estimates is passed, plots each of them stacked in its own panel. Plotting several estimates in one shared panel is not supported.

Requires ggplot2.
